subject: Request for red-team report and confirmation of remediation steps
messages:

Cc: legal@greenlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-02-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request for Red Team Report and Evidence of Fixes

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement review, our security team is requesting a copy of Redwood's most recent red-team/vulnerability assessment report (including full findings and test artifacts) and evidence that the highest-severity items have been remediated.

Could you please provide:
- The full report (all technical findings and appendices)
- A short mapping of remediation actions to each high/critical finding
- Any proof-of-fix artifacts (screenshots, logs, or Jira tickets) for priority items

If there are policy constraints on sharing the full report, please advise the acceptable alternatives and any paperwork (NDA) we need to sign. Our timeline is tight: procurement needs this by Feb 20 to keep the contract on schedule.

Thanks,
Daniel Liu
Head of Security Operations
Greenline Health

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Liu <daniel.liu@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request for Red Team Report and Evidence of Fixes

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the note and the timeline. Quick note up front: Redwood does not release full raw red-team/pen-testing reports externally due to tester confidentiality and third-party engagement terms. That said, we can support Greenline with three options that satisfy procurement and security review needs:

1) Controlled on-screen review (video call + screenshare) of the full report with our security team and only pre-approved attendees; no copies are provided and the session is recorded for your audit if desired.
2) A detailed executive summary that includes all high/critical findings (with technical context redacted) and a remediation mapping.
3) A remediation evidence bundle (screenshots, Jira/issue links, and test validation notes) that demonstrates fixes for high-severity items.

I've looped in our Security and Legal leads to help with the summary and to coordinate a controlled review if you prefer option 1. We can deliver the executive summary and remediation tracker by EOD Feb 13. For option 1 we would need a signed mutual NDA (we can share a one-page agreement) and a short attendee list in advance.

Which option would you like to proceed with?

Best,
Lauren Bishop

Lauren / team — attaching two artifacts:
- RA-executive-summary-Redwood-2026-02.pdf (executive summary with high/critical findings redacted to remove tester PII and exploitation scripts)
- remediation-tracker-Redwood-2026-02.csv (row-per-finding with status, owner, Jira ticket, and validation notes)

Summary highlights (excerpt):
- No findings that indicate customer data exfiltration or systemic cryptographic failures.
- Three high-severity findings (HT-101, HT-107, HT-119) related to misconfigured IAM policies, an exposed admin endpoint, and an outdated library causing dependency-level RCE risk. All three have fixes in place or scheduled as below.

Remediation status (short):
- HT-101 (IAM policy over-permissive): FIXED (deployment 2026-01-18) — validation: internal role audit + access logs attached. Jira: SEC-4423.
- HT-107 (admin endpoint access control): FIXED (2026-01-26) — validation: endpoint disabled for public access; access control tests passed. Jira: SEC-4479.
- HT-119 (outdated dependency): PARTIAL (backported security patch applied; full upgrade scheduled in 2/2026 release) — validation: dependency vulnerability mitigated for OWASP-critical vectors; final upgrade ticket: ENG-9120.

Notes on sharing: the raw test artifacts include tester tooling output and exploit code; per our third-party testing agreement we cannot distribute those artifacts. We can run a controlled on-screen review where the tester and Redwood security present details live. For procurement, the attached executive summary + remediation tracker are typically sufficient with an on-screen walkthrough.

I will also prepare a short pack of screenshots and log snippets (sanitized) to include in the evidence bundle. ETA for the sanitized evidence bundle: EOD Feb 13.

—Marissa
